491.t: Borrowed from Hebrew יְהוּדָה (yəhūḏāh) + the feminine form of -ιος (-ios, adjectival suffix).

498.t: From λογίζομαι (logízomai, “I calculate”) + -μός (-mós, verbal noun suffix).

484.t: Of unknown origin. A derivation from a Proto-Indo-European *gʰr-ono-, from *ǵʰer- (“to seize, enclose”), has been suggested, with original connotation of "encompassing time-limit".

451.t: Of disputed origin: * Maybe from Proto-Hellenic *twṓmə, from Proto-Indo-European *twoH-mn̥ (“compactness, swelling”), derived from *tewh₂- (“to swell”) + *-mn̥ (“nominal suffix”), and compared with σωρός (sōrós, “heap”).

493.t: Apheretic form of Ἀσσυρία (Assuría, “Assyria”), from Akkadian 𒀾𒋗𒊏𒅀 (Aššūrāyu), from 𒀸𒋩 (Aššur, “Assur”). The land corresponding to modern Syria was originally called Aram by its ancient inhabitants, the Arameans.

407.t: By surface analysis, ἐξ (ex, “out”) + -ατος (-ătos, superlative suffix), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *eǵʰs-katos. Compare with ἔγκατα (énkata, “intestines”) and the same difficulty in ἐχθός (ekhthós) = ἐκτός (ektós).

421.t: Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀩𐀺 (re-wo /⁠léwōn⁠/). Many ancient languages possessed similar words for lion, including Akkadian 𒌨 (labbu) (reconstructed to Proto-Semitic *labiʾ-).

470.t: From Proto-Hellenic *(h)méros; equivalent to μερ- (mer-), the root of μείρομαι (meíromai, “to receive as one's portion”) + -ος (-os).

441.t: From Biblical Hebrew שַׁבָּת (šabbāṯ, “Sabbath”), or, alternatively, from Aramaic שַׁבְּתָא (šabbəṯā, “Sabbath”).

494.t: From λόγος (lógos, “computation, reckoning”) + -ίζομαι (-ĭ́zomai, denominative mediopassive verb suffix).

446.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kərpós or *karpós, from Proto-Indo-European *kerp- (“pluck, harvest”), though debated whether via inheritance or borrowing from a different Indo-European branch due to the problematic α (a) in the Greek form.

423.t: From Proto-Indo-European *tridḱómt (“thirty”). Cognates include Latin trīgintā, Sanskrit त्रिंशत् (triṃśát) and Old Armenian երեսուն (eresun).

473.t: Superlative of the adverb ὕψι (hŭ́psĭ, “on high”).

480.t: From ὕψι (hŭ́psĭ, “aloft”), probably related to ὑπέρ (hupér, “above”).

499.t: From the zero-grade of Proto-Indo-European *sem- (“one”). The dative is from the PIE comitative-instrumental.

449.t: From Proto-Indo-European *penkʷēḱomth₂, from earlier *pénkʷedḱomt (“fifty”). Cognates include Latin quīnquāgintā, Sanskrit पञ्चाशत् (pañcāśát) and Old Armenian յիսուն (yisun).

439.t: From Proto-Hellenic *déyō, from Proto-Indo-European *dh₁yéti (“to bind”), from *deh₁- (“to bind”). Cognates include Sanskrit द्यति (dyati), Avestan 𐬥𐬍𐬛𐬌𐬌𐬁𐬙𐬄𐬨 (nīdiiātąm) and Albanian duaj.

413.t: From Proto-Hellenic *aná. Beekes' derivation from *h₂en- (“up, on high”) doesn't explain the second syllable.

472.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₃ésth₁. Cognates include Latin os, Sanskrit अस्थि (ásthi), Old Armenian ոսկր (oskr), and Albanian asht.

443.t: From Proto-Indo-European *nebʰ-el-h₂ (“cloud”). Related to νέφος (néphos, “cloud”), Latin nebula (“fog, cloud”).

402.t: From ἀ- (ă-, “without”, negative prefix) + δίκη (dĭ́kē, “justice”) + -ος (-os, adjective-forming suffix).

481.t: From Proto-Hellenic *nahwós, perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *nes- (“to join with, to conceal oneself”) and related to ναίω (naíō, “to dwell”), νέομαι (néomai, “to go or come back”).

489.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pleh₁- (“to fill”). See also πίμπλημι (pĭ́mplēmĭ, “to fill”).

408.t: From Proto-Hellenic *gʷous (compare Mycenaean Greek 𐀦𐀃 (qo-o /⁠gʷōns⁠/)), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷṓws. Cognates include Old English cū (English cow), Irish bó, Latin bōs, and Sanskrit गो (gó).

469.t: From Proto-Hellenic *gʷlépō, of unclear further origin.

492.t: Of unclear origin. Perhaps from a Proto-Indo-European *wr̥b-, with cognates such as Lithuanian virbas, Old Church Slavonic врьба (vrĭba) (Russian верба (verba)) and Latin verbēnae.

454.t: From ὅς (hós, “who, which”, relative pronoun) + τις (tĭs, “someone, anyone”, indefinite pronoun).

495.t: From πρό (pró, “before”) + -τερος (-teros, contrastive or comparative suffix).

464.t: Uncertain. Mechanically reconstructable as a thematization of a nasal present *pl-néh₂-ti, corresponding to Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat, broad”), but the semantics are highly problematic.

486.t: PIE word *wek⁽ʷ⁾speros Ellipsis of ἑσπέρα ὥρα (hespérā hṓrā, “time of evening”), from ἕσπερος (hésperos, “of evening, western”).

436.t: Likely from Proto-Indo-European *dʰewH- (“to shake, move violently”), though Beekes expresses semantic doubts. Cognate to Sanskrit धू॒नोति॑ (dhūnóti, “to shake; to move to and fro quickly”) and Old Norse dýja (“to shake”).

405.t: Of disputed origin: * Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂-, a metathesized form of *kelh₂- (“to hit, cut down”).

477.t: From Proto-Indo-European *kʷís. Compare its interrogative form ποῦ (poû).

496.t: According to Beekes, since it is highly probable that πτώξ (ptṓx, “hare”) is related (with original meaning "who ducks away, the shy one"), it is probably a Pre-Greek word, in view of the alternation χ/κ.

485.t: Perhaps from Proto-Hellenic *wewortā́ and related to ἐρίηρoς (eríēros), ἔρανος (éranos), ἦρα (êra), with further cognates outside Hellenic unknown.

482.t: From προφήτης (prophḗtēs, “prophet”) from πρόφημι (próphēmi, “to speak beforehand”).

460.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hébdomos, from Proto-Indo-European *septm̥mós (“seventh”), with medial voicing (the -bd- cluster) perhaps by influence from the following nasal.

401.t: From Proto-Indo-European *twós; cognate with Vedic Sanskrit त्व (tvá) and Old Armenian քո (kʻo).

409.t: Stems: * κλαϝ- > κλα- (κλάω (klā́ō)) / κλαυ- (κλαυ-θμός (klau-thmós)) * κλαϝ-j- > κλαι- * κλαϝ-σ- > κλαυσ- (the future κλαύσω (klaúsō), κλαυσι-) * κλαϝ-ε- > κλαϝ-ε-σ- > the future κλαήσω (klaḗsō). Uncertain etymology.

463.t: From δια- (dĭă-, “in different directions, apart, asunder; dia-”) + βαίνω (baínō, “to walk, step”).

434.t: Traditionally considered a contamination of ἄμαθος (ắmăthos, “sand”) and ψάμμος (psắmmos, “sand”).

430.t: From ὅς (hós) + τε (te). Compare τότε (tóte), πότε (póte), ποτέ (poté).

412.t: From μή (mḗ, “not”) + δέ (dé, “and, but”). Compare οὐδέ (oudé, “but not, and not”).

461.t: According to Beekes and LIV, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷel(h₃)- (“to want, wish”) (with no certain cognates), but with unexplained and pervasive o-grade in the present.

410.t: From παρα- (pără-, “by, near”) + ἔρχομαι (érkhomai, “to come, go”).

428.t: From ἐκεῖ (ekeî, “yonder”) + -θεν (-then, “from”). This is the expected distal source demonstrative reflex.

445.t: Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀁𐀚𐀏 (e-ne-ka); otherwise unknown. Formerly thought a composite of ἕν (hén) and *ϝέκα (*wéka) (see: ἑκών (hekṓn)).

418.t: From ἐκ- (ek-, “out”) + λέγω (légō, “to choose”). Exact cognate in form and meaning to Latin ēligō (“to choose”).

420.t: From Αἴγυπτος (Aígŭptos) + -ιος (-ĭos). Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐁁𐀓𐀠𐀴𐀍 (a3-ku-pi-ti-jo).

444.t: πρῶτος (prôtos, “first”) + τίκτω (tíktō, “to beget”) + -ος (-os), with a passive meaning. Compare the paroxytonic form πρωτοτόκος (prōtotókos), with an active meaning.

425.t: From δικαιόω (dikaióō, “to set right, deem right”) + -μα (-mă).

466.t: According to Beekes, probably of Pre-Greek origin, due to the lack of clear cognates.

475.t: Hellenistic noun from ancient verb βδελύσσομαι (bdelússomai)/βδελύττομαι (bdelúttomai, “to be disgusted; despise”) (stem: *βδελύτj (*bdelútj)) from adjective βδελυρός (bdelŭrós) from *βδελυλός (*bdelulós), which originates from the verb βδέω (bdéō, “fart”)…

411.t: From ἐξ- (ex-, “ex-, out-”) + αἱρέω (hairéō, “to take, seize”).

429.t: ἐπι- (epi-, “epi-, on-”) + σκέπτομαι (sképtomai, “to look at, examine”).
